evidence.finding: Routing configuration version 24.7 was deployed to all queues at 09:15, matching the incident start exactly.
Aggregate transfer rate increased abruptly from approximately 6% before deployment to 13.49% at 09:15 and remained near 13% through 11:45.
AHT rose from 376.55 seconds at 09:00 to 527.91 seconds at 09:15 and remained roughly 498–535 seconds afterward, materially reducing throughput.
Service level fell from 88.24% at 09:00 to 44.71% at 09:15 and remained below the 80% target for every subsequent interval.
ASA increased from 33.75 seconds at 09:00 to 80.91 seconds at 09:15 and remained elevated, reaching 94.23 seconds at 10:30.

At deployment, all queues showed simultaneous transfer-rate and AHT increases, with service levels falling to 52.78% in General Service, 40.91% in Billing, 36.84% in Account Support and 37.5% in Escalations.
All 49 scheduled agents remained logged in throughout the window, while productive staffing stayed within 44–46 agents and training remained zero.
Volume was moderately above forecast after deployment—for example, 88 versus 79 calls at 09:15 and 95 versus 78 at 10:30—adding pressure but not accounting for the abrupt transfer and AHT shifts.
From 09:15 onward, answered calls consistently trailed offered calls, with 13–31 abandons in most intervals and occupancy frequently at 100%, demonstrating sustained congestion.

primary_root_cause_detail: Routing configuration version 24.7 was deployed at 09:15, exactly when transfer rates and AHT increased across all queues. The resulting loss of throughput drove sustained queueing, higher ASA and service-level degradation despite stable staffing. Moderately above-forecast volume amplified the impact but does not explain the abrupt, deployment-aligned operational shift.
recommended_actions: Roll back or disable routing configuration version 24.7 and verify recovery of transfer rate, AHT, ASA and service level by queue.
Compare version 24.7 with the prior routing configuration, focusing on skill mappings, transfer rules, escalation paths and unintended routing loops.
Run pre-production call-path tests and transfer-rate guardrails before redeployment, with automatic rollback thresholds tied to AHT, transfers and service level.
Use temporary overflow routing or cross-skilled staffing to drain accumulated demand while the configuration is corrected.
Review forecast variance and add short-term staffing flexibility for moderate above-forecast volume, while keeping this separate from remediation of the primary routing defect.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Actual volume was moderately above forecast in several intervals, but the increases were insufficient to explain the immediate doubling of transfer rates and roughly 40% AHT increase exactly at deployment.
Scheduled and logged-in staffing remained fixed at 49, and productive staffing stayed within its pre-incident range.

AHT was a major mechanism of service degradation, but its simultaneous onset with the routing deployment and transfer-rate jump supports treating it as a downstream effect rather than the deepest cause.
Adherence remained approximately 90–94%, consistent with pre-incident levels, with no sustained decline at 09:15.
No agents were in training during any interval.
Degradation and transfer increases appeared across all queues rather than being isolated to one mismatched queue, and queue staffing did not change.
No platform event was reported; the only corroborating operational event was the routing deployment.
Forecast misses contributed some excess demand, but performance deteriorated abruptly through transfer and handling changes even where actual volume was close to forecast.
The reported service-level values reconcile with the supplied formula, and offered calls reconcile with answered plus abandoned calls.

stakeholder_summary: The incident was caused by routing configuration version 24.7. Its 09:15 deployment coincided exactly with a broad transfer-rate increase, sharply higher AHT and sustained service-level failure across all queues. Staffing remained stable; moderately elevated volume increased the severity but was not the primary cause.
